title: Fock-state preparation based on amplitude amplification in cavity QED
authors: Sharoon Austin, Zhi-Yuan Wei, Kartik Srinivasan, Alexey V. Gorshkov
abstract: In this work, we develop a coherent control technique for cavity QED based on amplitude amplification. We consider two physical platforms. In the first setting, we study a three-level quantum emitter coupled to a single mode of an optical cavity and introduce a protocol for producing traveling single photons based on oblivious amplitude amplification. As the key ingredient of our protocol, we propose an extension of oblivious amplitude amplification which uses reflection unitaries solely on the signal qubit, along with $U$ and $U^\dagger$, where the unitary $U$ prepares the initial state. Our approach improves the scaling of the single-photon-generation protocol length from $N\sim 1/p$ to $N\sim 1/\sqrt{p}$, with $p$ denoting the success probability of obtaining a short single photon from a single application of the weak control pulse. Furthermore, our protocol also reduces the error from intrinsic cavity loss compared to protocols using a single strong control pulse in various experimentally relevant regimes, suggesting the application of our methods for error reduction. In the second setting, we consider a superconducting qubit coupled to a single bosonic mode of a microwave cavity in a circuit QED architecture in the dispersive regime for preparing Fock states. Using fixed-point amplitude amplification, we obtain a protocol for preparing Fock states whose length scales as $O(n^{1/4})$, where $n$ is the number of photons. Additionally, as an application of our methods for state preparation, we describe a protocol for preparing NOON states.
summary: The paper presents advanced coherent control techniques using amplitude amplification to enhance single-photon sources and prepare multi-photon Fock states in both optical and microwave cavity QED systems. Key achievements include improving the scaling of photon generation protocols and achieving state preparation with $O(n^{1/4})$ length scaling. This work is highly relevant for experimental quantum optics aiming for scalable quantum information processing.
main_problem: The work develops coherent control techniques based on amplitude amplification to achieve high-efficiency single-photon sources and prepare arbitrary Fock states in cavity QED.
main_result: A protocol for single-photon generation improves scaling from $N \sim 1/p$ to $N \sim 1/\sqrt{p}$, while Fock state preparation scales as $O(n^{1/4})$.
method: The core method involves extending oblivious amplitude amplification and utilizing fixed-point amplitude amplification within the framework of cavity QED dynamics.
model_or_system: Two platforms are studied: a three-level quantum emitter coupled to an optical cavity for photon sources, and a superconducting qubit coupled to a microwave cavity in circuit QED for Fock state preparation. The dynamics are governed by coupled differential equations describing the interaction Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Single-photon retrieval efficiency ($\eta_2$), single-photon loss ($1-\eta_3$), and fidelity of prepared states (e.g., NOON states).
important_parameters: Success probability $p$, number of photons $n$, coupling strength $g$, cavity decay rate $\kappa$, and intrinsic loss rates ($\kappa_i, \gamma$).
main_assumptions: The analysis often relies on the weak control pulse limit or the adiabatic approximation for long Grover sequences to simplify error analysis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate system setups (atom/cavity coupling) and plot performance metrics like inefficiency ($1-\eta_2$) versus sequence length parameter $k$ in both lossless and lossy regimes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops the theory by first introducing the general amplitude amplification framework, then applying it to single-photon generation (addressing scaling improvements and losses), followed by its application to Fock state preparation using fixed-point methods, and concluding with detailed error analysis for both scenarios.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, scalable protocols for generating fundamental quantum resources (single photons, high-number Fock states) essential for quantum networking and computation, directly addressing practical limitations like loss and scaling in cavity QED.
